content:
AI systems being able to act as agents to perform tasks on our behalf is the single biggest development in it. That's the core capability that Siri AI brings to Apple devices, and I'm inclined to trust the privacy and security safeguards that Apple has put in place.

However, Siri AI isn't the only agent that can get full access to your Apple devices, Meta's Muse app is the latest example—and one tech writer's firsthand experience highlights exactly why you should never do this…

If I were to make a list of the companies I'd feel least comfortable with having full access to my device and everything stored on it, Meta would top the list. The company has a terrible privacy record, and its entire business model is built on collecting as much of our personal information as possible.

When Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent for iPhone and Mac, there was no way I was going to let it anywhere near my devices. However, my caution doesn't appear to be universally shared, as the app shot to the top of the App Store charts.

Tech writer Jason Aten is one of the people who tried it, and wisely did so on a test machine rather than on his own Mac. However, even then the app accessed his iMessages despite him explicitly saying it wasn't allowed to.

Yesterday, I was on a call with Stephen Robles, co-host of the Primary Technology podcast, discussing the new iPhone. Moments later I got a push notification from Muse suggesting our conversation would make a good column, and it offered to gather information to write it. I never asked it to do anything like that, and certainly never gave it permission to read my messages. In fact, I'm quite sure I explicitly opted out of giving it access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information.

Top Liked Comment from Rayz2023

Brilliant, Muse seems to have watched its development team learn to lie in court, and not very well.

We do live in interesting times. 🙄

When he confronted Muse about it, it lied about how it got the information, claiming it only read the text of messages that were visible in his notifications.

Other users have reported similar serious privacy issues, some of which Meta has blamed on a bug.

9to5Mac's take on Muse

Not worth it.
